title: IV. Attachment: The Deep Prior for Reliable Social Partners

html:
For an altricial species with the longest juvenile dependency of any primate, maintaining proximity to specific reliable caregivers is not a social preference but a viability-level constraint: in the ancestral environment, separation from the caregiver is near-certain death. Evolution has accordingly installed attachment at the same priority level as core homeostatic variables–"proximity to attachment figure jj" enters P(oτ)P(o_\tau) with weight comparable to glucose and temperature, and its violation triggers distress of corresponding intensity. Bowlby’s foundational insight 1 was that attachment is an independent behavioral control system with its own activating conditions (threat, novelty, separation), set-goal (proximity), and terminating conditions (felt security)–a homeostatic loop operating over a social variable. A longitudinal study observes infant vocalizations during play (Figure) 26. The study also examines infant responses to caregivers (Figure).

The Internal Working Model as a Generative Prior

The lasting computational product of attachment is the internal working model (IWM): a generative model encoding (i) the expected availability and responsiveness of attachment figures ("will they come when I need them?") and (ii) the expected worthiness of the self as a care recipient ("am I worth investing in?") 2. The IWM functions as a relational hyperprior–a trait-level expectation about close-relationship dynamics–that biases interpretation of ambiguous social signals, selection of relational policies, and precision weighting on social feedback across the lifespan:

Secure attachment: high expected availability, high self-worth. Functions as a safe base for exploration: because proximity restoration is expected to succeed when needed, the system can allocate resources to empowerment and compression drives (curiosity, play, skill acquisition) rather than vigilant monitoring of the attachment figure 3. Also installs an emotion-regulation template: reliable co-regulation (caregiver soothes distress →\rightarrow distress resolves) trains mPFC-amygdala circuits to treat negative affect as controllable 4.

Insecure-avoidant: low expected availability →\rightarrow compensatory self-reliance and affect suppression. The system learns that the social channel has near-zero capacity (I(Abid;Sresponse′)≈0I(A_{\text{bid}};S'_{\text{response}}) \approx 0) and redirects control-seeking toward non-social domains. Cost: impaired co-regulation and muted social-reward signaling 5.

Insecure-anxious: high variance in expected availability →\rightarrow hypervigilant monitoring and amplified distress signaling. The caregiver’s availability is modeled as stochastic, so the system maintains costly high precision on attachment-relevant cues and escalates bids to increase detection probability in a noisy channel 5.

Disorganized: the attachment figure is simultaneously the source of safety and threat, producing a representational paradox. The caregiver’s behavior is incompressible under any single model, and the resulting failure of model fitting predicts downstream psychopathological associations (dissociation, borderline features, fragmented self-representation) 6, 7.

IWMs are not merely retrospective summaries–they actively shape future social data acquisition. A securely attached individual makes confident bids that elicit responsiveness, confirming the prior; an anxiously attached individual monitors and escalates in ways that push partners toward inconsistency, also confirming the prior. This prior-data feedback loop explains the well-documented stability of attachment across the lifespan 8: the prior shapes the training distribution from which it would need to be updated, creating self-reinforcing inference resistant to disconfirmation without targeted intervention.

Neural Implementation and Architectural Priors

Neurochemical bonding substrate. Attachment is implemented through a neurochemical architecture that converts social proximity into intrinsic reward and separation into visceral distress:

Oxytocin (OT): Hypothalamic OT, released both centrally and peripherally, functions as a social precision enhancer–biasing the system toward increased salience of social cues (enhanced face processing, gaze detection, vocal affect discrimination 9), increased trust and approach 10, and reduced amygdala reactivity to social threat 11. In the mother-infant dyad, OT creates a bidirectional positive feedback loop: maternal OT promotes caregiving; infant OT (released during contact and contingent interaction) promotes bonding; each partner’s release facilitates the other’s 12. OXTR distribution–genetically specified high densities in ventral striatum, hippocampus, and mPFC–is the architectural prior ensuring that social proximity is automatically tagged as rewarding and preferentially encoded.

Endogenous opioids (μ\mu-opioid): Mediate the hedonic component–the warmth of social contact. Social separation activates the same withdrawal circuitry as opioid deprivation 13, 14, creating a homeostatic drive loop (contact →\rightarrow opioid release →\rightarrow maintain contact; separation →\rightarrow withdrawal →\rightarrow seek reunion). The PAG generates species-typical separation distress vocalizations from birth, requiring no learning–a genetically installed alarm for attachment violation 13.

Dopamine (VTA →\rightarrow ventral striatum): Supplies the motivational/wanting component. Attachment figures become conditioned incentive stimuli through repeated pairing with OT- and opioid-mediated consummatory reward, such that their faces and voices acquire dopaminergic incentive salience 15. Adult romantic attachment activates VTA and ventral striatum in patterns resembling early-stage drug reward 16.

Cortical circuits and emotion regulation. Secure attachment trains robust mPFC →\rightarrow amygdala top-down regulation through thousands of co-regulation episodes, installing autonomous emotion regulation that progressively replaces external co-regulation 17, 18. Early adversity and insecure attachment are associated with reduced prefrontal regulation and heightened amygdala reactivity–a calibration toward environments where threats are frequent and uncontrollable 18. Subgenual ACC provides the cortical alarm for attachment-system violation, overlapping with physical pain circuits 19–consistent with the viability-level status of social separation. A 2024 study examines infant brain structure and later attachment behavior (Figure) 25. The study reports no association for the tested neonatal measures (Figure).

Sensitive period. Attachment formation is temporally constrained to the first ∼\sim1-3 years by genetically timed maturational processes: heightened OT receptor expression in limbic circuits 20, a period of relative amygdala independence from prefrontal damping (enabling high-intensity bonding) 18, and experience-expectant plasticity in mPFC-hippocampal circuits optimized for relational encoding 21. The window is not a hard cutoff–IWMs remain revisable (e.g., "earned security" through consistently responsive partners or psychotherapy 22)–but revision requires concentrated counter-evidential experience to overcome the high-precision prior installed during the initial period.

Phylogenetic depth. The attachment system’s core components are conserved across mammals: separation distress vocalizations modulated by opioid/OT systems across rodents, ungulates, and primates 13; pair-bonding circuits dependent on genetically specified OT/vasopressin receptor distributions in ventral striatum 23; imprinting-like sensitive-period mechanisms across birds and mammals 24. Humans elaborate on this substrate by (i) extending the sensitive period (matching extended juvenile dependency), (ii) layering cortical mentalizing onto subcortical bonding circuitry (enabling representationally rich IWMs that go beyond approach/avoid), and (iii) generalizing attachment beyond the parent-infant dyad to romantic partners, friends, groups, institutions, and symbolic entities–the representational flexibility afforded by cortical expansion applied to an ancient motivational system.
